question.text: A frictionless pulley is fixed to a ceiling. A light string that does not stretch passes over it: a 2 kg block hangs from one end. From the other end the string leads down to a 4 kg block; a second light string then connects the 4 kg block to a 6 kg block hanging below it. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the acceleration of the system and the tension in each of the two strings.
conditions: string is massless and does not stretch
the 4 kg and 6 kg blocks move down together while the 2 kg block moves up

figure.description: A single fixed pulley hangs from the ceiling. A string over the pulley holds a 2 kg block on one side, moving upward with acceleration a. On the other side, the string (tension T₁) runs down to a 4 kg block; a second string (tension T₂) hangs below the 4 kg block and connects it to a 6 kg block. The 4 kg and 6 kg blocks move downward together with acceleration a.

solution.approach: The 4 kg and 6 kg blocks move together as one 10 kg mass on the heavier side of the pulley, giving a plain two-mass pulley problem.

steps.text: The 2 kg block goes up and the combined 4 kg + 6 kg = 10 kg goes down with the same acceleration a.
Put in g = 10 m/s² and solve.
T₁ is the tension pulling the 2 kg block up, so apply Newton's second law to it.
Put in a = 20/3 m/s² and solve for T₁.
T₂ is the tension pulling the 6 kg block up from below the 4 kg block, so apply Newton's second law to the 6 kg block.
Put in a = 20/3 m/s² and solve for T₂.
steps.why_this_step: The 6 kg block feels only its own weight down and T₂ up, since nothing hangs below it.

common_mistakes.text: Forgetting the 4 kg block and taking the heavier side as only 6 kg, giving a = (6−2)×10/8 = 5 m/s².
Treating the 6 kg block as not accelerating and taking T₂ = 6g = 60 N.
